raw_response:
I'm 78 this year, and my old bones don't move like they used to. Just me and my old man — two mouths to feed on 10 mu of land. I never went to school, not one day, but I've been farming this dirt for 35 years and I know it better than my own hands. We get by on the farm income and that little rural pension, 128 yuan a month, so every yuan I spend has to come back to me.

My wheat is already in the ground. I planted it last October, around the 10th, same as always. I used my own saved seed mixed with some I bought from Old Wang's shop in the village — that way it only costs me about 15 yuan per mu for the new seed. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu on the 7 mu. That's what I've always done. Now it's late April and the wheat is jointing, so I need to topdress with urea. I spread about half a bag per mu — I don't weigh it, I sling it by hand until it looks right. Last year I skimped a bit and the wheat turned yellow, so this year I'm putting the full half bag. I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than lose yield. I already watered once before winter, and I'll water two more times: now, and once when the grain is filling. The well pump costs electricity, about 40 yuan each time for the whole 7 mu. It hurts to pay it, but dry wheat means no harvest.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, mid-June. You can't waste a single day — sometimes the combine harvests wheat in the morning and we plant maize that same afternoon. I buy hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu, costs around 45 yuan. I put compound fertilizer in the planting hole, same as wheat, about one bag per mu. If the summer rains are good I might not topdress, but if the leaves turn yellow when it's knee-high, I'll spread a bit of urea. I water maize once or twice in summer, only if it's very dry. Usually the rain is enough, and I save on the pump.

Cotton is on my 3 mu on the south side. I plant it now, around April 20th-25th. Cotton is heavy work — thinning, spraying, picking. My back can't handle the picking anymore, so I hire the village women for 100 yuan a day plus lunch. That's my biggest cost, but what can I do? I put less fertilizer on cotton than wheat, about three-quarters of a bag of compound per mu, and a little urea when it flowers. I spray for bollworms three times — I watch the fields and when I see the moths I mix the medicine. I water cotton twice: at flowering and when the bolls are forming.

Money is tight. I don't buy the fancy seed or the expensive fertilizer — the regular shop stuff is fine. I don't take risks. If I'm not sure, I do what I did last year. Last year was decent: wheat gave me about 900 jin per mu, maize about 1000 jin. I'm hoping for about the same this year, maybe a bit less for cotton because the hired help isn't as careful as me.
